parts.partSubtitle: A study of motion, forces, and energy.

units.title: Kinematics: Describing Motion
units.coreIdea: Motion can be described and predicted using mathematical relationships between position, velocity, and acceleration.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: The motion of a launched projectile, such as a water bottle rocket.

units.title: Dynamics: Forces and Newton's Laws
units.coreIdea: Forces cause changes in motion, and their relationship is described by Newton's laws.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: A skydiver falling from a plane and reaching terminal velocity.

parts.partSubtitle: The principles of conservation of energy and momentum.

units.title: Conservation of Energy
units.coreIdea: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed.
keySkills: Applying the law of conservation of energy
units.anchoringPhenomenon: A rollercoaster car's motion as it navigates hills and loops.

units.title: Conservation of Momentum
units.coreIdea: The total momentum of a closed system remains constant.
keySkills: Solving elastic and inelastic collision problems
units.anchoringPhenomenon: Two pool balls colliding on a table, changing their directions and speeds.

parts.partSubtitle: Exploring periodic motion, sound, and electricity.

units.title: Waves and Sound
units.coreIdea: Waves are a mechanism for energy transfer through a medium.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: A vibrating string on a guitar producing different musical notes.

units.title: Electricity and Magnetism
units.coreIdea: Electric and magnetic forces are two aspects of a single electromagnetic interaction.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: How a simple electric motor works.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Water Bottle Rocket Launch
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Analyze the motion of a water bottle rocket from launch to landing, including its maximum height and range.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Video footage of the rocket launch with time stamps, initial pressure and water volume data.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Skydiver's Fall
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Use free-body diagrams and Newton's laws to explain why a skydiver's velocity changes and then becomes constant.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Velocity-time graph for the skydiver's descent and their mass.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Rollercoaster Dynamics
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Investigate the energy transformations of a frictionless rollercoaster, and then account for energy loss due to friction.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Track height data at various points and mass of the rollercoaster car.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Collision of Pool Balls
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Analyze the velocities of two pool balls before and after a collision to determine if momentum is conserved.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Video of a collision with position and time tracking data for both balls.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Guitar String Vibration
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Explain how different notes are produced on a guitar string by changing the string's length or tension, and how a standing wave is formed.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Videos of a guitar string vibrating at different frequencies.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Simple Electric Circuit
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Design and build a simple circuit with a battery, switch, and light bulb. Analyze how current, voltage, and resistance interact.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Resistors of various values and a voltmeter/ammeter.

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Electric Motor
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Investigate how a simple electric motor works by using the principles of electromagnetism to produce rotational motion.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: A simple motor kit with wire, magnets, and a battery.
